summary: The two Python additions (ai-os-scripts/phase4_finalize_terminology_exemptions.py and the --suggest-fix mode added to ai-os/TERMINOLOGY_GUARDRAIL_2026-07-24.py) are well-scoped, additive, and reasonably careful: the finalizer fails loudly (raises) rather than guessing a disposition for an unmapped (file, category) pair, and --suggest-fix never writes to source files, only enriches a JSON report for human review. No command injection, eval, or unsafe file-path handling was found in either script. However, the diff also adds compliance-tracker-work as a bare git gitlink (mode 160000, commit dd159cc1406cb816760c11e8386141e112c3b245) with no accompanying .gitmodules file anywhere in the repo. Inspecting the working tree confirms this is a full nested clone of the entire compliance-tracker project (AGENTS.md, ai-os/, drizzle/, bun.lock, etc.) that the worker apparently checked out into its workspace as scratch space, which then got swept into the automated checkpoint commit as an orphan gitlink. This is unrelated to the task's stated scope (terminology exemption migration), is not registered as a real submodule, and would leave the repo in a broken/confusing state for any future clone (an empty placeholder directory with a dangling, unregistered commit reference). This is real accidental noise that should not land in main history and blocks approval as-is; the task should be resubmitted after `git rm --cached compliance-tracker-work` (and the nested clone deleted from the workspace) so the diff contains only the two legitimate Phase 4 script additions.
issues: compliance-tracker-work is committed as a dangling git gitlink (mode 160000) pointing at commit dd159cc1406cb816760c11e8386141e112c3b245 with no .gitmodules entry anywhere in the repo -- confirmed via `git ls-tree HEAD compliance-tracker-work` and inspecting the working directory, which shows a full nested clone of the unrelated compliance-tracker project (AGENTS.md, ai-os/, drizzle/, bun.lock, etc.), not a real submodule. This is workspace scratch content accidentally swept in by the automated checkpoint commit and must be removed before merge (git rm --cached compliance-tracker-work + delete the nested clone from the workspace).
